instructions: Fresh review of each primary candidate: read dialogue first, then exact cards. Assess all six unchanged criteria and all coach-2.0 gates with turn-specific evidence. For pairs, show whether the Stance changes HOW A pursues the Drive in one interaction. Do not invent missing backstory or assume prior approval. Use the alternate only to assess meaningful differentiation. Report actual reservations. No writer scores or improvement claims are supplied.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Carry This with Me
cards.instruction: Get someone to share a burden by framing participation as part of the relationship.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. Take half Mum's care-home forms. Being her children can't mean I'm the paperwork child.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You understand them better.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. Then sit beside me. I'll explain, and you can write.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: All right. It asks for one main contact.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Put yourself. I'll help with every answer, but Mum needs to know she can reach either of us.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've assigned us this box of letters before the removal van comes. We wrote them together; we're sorting them together.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You kept them. I thought you'd want to decide.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I haven't approved making me the keeper of all ten years. You may choose what matters beside me, not leave me to choose for both of us.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll take the box, but I can't read them today.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Postponement granted. Before you take the box, set a date for us to open it together. I'm not transferring all the deciding to you either.

cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: What Are We Now?
cards.instruction: Find out how someone defines the relationship without directly asking for a label.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before I approve our booking for your sister's wedding, present your room plan. One room or two?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: One is cheaper.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Economy approved. Double bed, or are you requesting twins?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Twins. I don't want to confuse things.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Twins approved. Now the breakfast arrangement: am I sitting with your family, or waiting for you in the lobby? I want that settled before I authorize the booking.

cards.title: Take My Side
cards.instruction: Recruit someone into your interpretation of a conflict involving a shared relationship.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. When Mum mentions the holiday argument, remind her I offered to drive.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: After you lost the tickets.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. We can build toward that detail.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm telling the whole story.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Start at the helpful bit so the rest has context.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're Alex's friend too. I've chosen you to explain that alternating allotment weekends is a fair compromise.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: All three of us agreed to go every Saturday.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You may mention the old arrangement after you've explained that my version shares the workload.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll talk to him, but you have to admit you changed it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That admission is approved. Put it this way: I changed the rota because I want us to stay friends. I want him hearing that from someone who knows us both.

cards.title: Prove We’re Close
cards.instruction: Get someone to take a social or emotional risk that demonstrates trust in the connection.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've decided we should arrive at the reunion holding hands. I want us to trust each other in that room.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They still think we're just friends. Are you sure?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I approve correcting them. You may keep hold even if someone stares.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Last time someone asked, you let go. You introduce me this time.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Agreed. I'm assigning myself the introduction: 'This is my partner.' Then you may hold me to it, literally. Will you come in with me?

beats.text: I haven't approved another 'fine.' Send the awkward version you deleted; I want us to trust each other with it.

cards.title: Acknowledge Our History
cards.instruction: Make someone recognize that the relationship, memory, or sacrifice mattered and cannot be treated as incidental.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I haven't approved boxing our allotment photo. That summer deserves more than the back of a cupboard.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We grew three carrots. I need the shelf.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I approve freeing the shelf, not calling it wasted. You got out of bed every morning to water those carrots with me.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I could put the photo on my desk at work.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That move is approved. When someone laughs at the harvest, tell them about those mornings. I'm not authorizing a caption that makes it just three carrots.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm not approving the bin for our ferry ticket. Remember the overtime we worked for that weekend.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We missed the ferry. I hate being reminded.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You may hate the ferry. We stayed anyway; that was the first time we chose each other over a refund.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Let's keep the hotel receipt in an envelope instead. That part was lovely.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Substitution approved. Write 'that part was lovely' on the envelope in your handwriting. I want a record that it mattered to you too.
